name: Question 6
problem:
Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}-14 & 12 & 3 \\ -20 & 17 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2.$
worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =2.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-14 & 12 & 3 \\ -20 & 17 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-16 & 12 & 3 \\ -20 & 15 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-16{x}_{1}+12{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ -20{x}_{1}+15{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=0 \\ -{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-16 & 12 & 3 & 0 \\ -20 & 15 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-\frac{5}{4}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-16 & 12 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{4} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-16 & 12 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{4} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this in the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=\frac{3}{4}{x}_{2}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=4,$ we get the eigenvector
$v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

Question 6

Find an eigenvector of A=[−14123−20174001] that corresponds to the eigenvalue λ=2.

b
[45−1]

Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation (A−λI)x=0.

In our case, we have λ=2. So, we obtain

A−λI=[−14123−20174001]−2[100010001]=[−16123−2015400−1].

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

{−16x1+12x2+3x3=0−20x1+15x2+4x3=0−x3=0

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix M to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

M=[−161230−20154000−10]R2:=R2+(−54)R1∼[−1612300014000−10]R3:=R3+4R2∼[−161230001400000]

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the 1st and the 3rd). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain x3=0. Substituting this in the first equation, we get x1=34x2. Therefore, the general solution is [34x2x20],x2∈R.

Setting, for instance, x2=4, we get the eigenvector v=[340].
